Step-1   What happens in the metathesis  
With a second–generation Grubbs catalyst two molecules of a terminal alkene R-CH=CH2 undergo self-metathesis to give

R-CH=CH-R  +  CH2=CH2  

Ethene is to be ignored, so only the dimer R-CH=CH-R is relevant.

For 3-methylpent-1-ene  
R = CH3-CH2-CH(CH3)-CH2-  
(the carbon bearing the Me group is stereogenic, so the starting alkene is obtained as a racemate).

Step-2   Skeleton of the only metathesis product  
Dimerisation gives the C10 alkene

CH3CH2CH(CH3)CH2-CH=CH-CH2CH(CH3)CH2CH3

No other C–C connectivity is produced in simple self-metathesis of a single terminal alkene, so every possible product has this skeleton.

Step-3   Stereochemical possibilities  
a) Geometry of the C=C bond  
   • E (trans)  
   • Z (cis)

b) Configuration at the two stereogenic centres (one on each side of the double bond)  
   • R,R and S,S  → a racemic (dl) pair  
   • R,S (or S,R) → a meso form

Thus, for each alkene geometry there are two distinguishable products:
   • racemic dl pair (optically inactive because present 1:1)  
   • meso form (internally achiral)

Step-4   Counting products  
Because the question asks for “possible products”, it is standard to regard an enantiomeric pair obtained in racemic form as a single product (just as racemic 2-chlorobutane is usually counted as one product in an S N 1 reaction).

Therefore:
   • E-meso
   • E-racemic (dl)
   • Z-meso
   • Z-racemic (dl)

Total distinct products (excluding ethene) = 4.

Answer: C
